description: An international consortium of academic bioethics institutes and open-source AI developers launches a voluntary 'BioGuard' initiative, embedding tamper-resistant watermarking and use-tracking into widely used open biology models. The system is not legally binding but gains rapid adoption due to community pressure and integration into major model hubs. It represents a bottom-up attempt to impose safety norms in the absence of effective regulation, and could slow misuse if it becomes a de facto standard — though it is easily bypassed by determined actors with sufficient compute.
